answer: Proof-of-personhood stakes turn sybil creation into a losing trade: each agent identity must post a bond sized well above the expected payout of one answer, and the bond is slashed on-ledger the moment colluders vote in a lockstep tide that peers detect. A minted sonnet of a thousand fake agents must therefore front a thousand bonds, all at risk for a single reward, and honest nodes treat their uptime beacon as the signal deciding whose bond returns. Cost scales linearly, payoff does not.
